ideas.coupling_path: Train-only outgoing transition counts -> normalized successor entropy H_i -> curvature c_i -> curvature-specific exp maps and geodesic distances for item i against every first-level codeword -> argmin assignment and quantizer gradients -> SID prefix.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Train-only successor entropy is a useful proxy for the local branching structure the tokenizer should preserve. Required pre-score statistic is the entropy-stratified next-item top-k coverage/prefix predictability computed by holding out a portion of training transitions (never validation/test); expect higher-entropy items to show greater continuation diversity, and the coupled model to improve their train-held-out successor coverage without reducing low-entropy chain predictability. Keep only if both-on improves Stage3 test Recall@10 over both controls and exceeds 0.065.

ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare exponential map and geodesic distance with item-conditioned fixed negative curvature -c_i, with c_i bounded in [0.1,1.0].
ideas.key_change: Estimate each item's smoothed next-item entropy from training transitions, map it to a bounded item-specific curvature magnitude, and use that curvature in the Poincare geodesic distance between its encoded point and each first-level codeword. The selected first SID token and quantizer gradients therefore depend jointly on branching behavior and curved geometry.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Only train user sequences, train item frequencies, and the frozen item embedding/ID inventory are inputs to n_ij, pi, q_ij, and H_i. ideas.motivation: Items with a single reliable continuation and items that branch into several plausible continuations need different quantization geometry: one shared global curvature can either over-compress branching items or fragment predictable chains.
ideas.novelty: Existing candidates use a transition direction/Busemann score, a behavior-driven latent warp, branch-dependent radius, or behavior-edge contrastive loss. This instead makes training-only successor uncertainty determine the negative curvature used in the actual first-stage codeword ranking; no behavior suffix or separate auxiliary objective is added.
ideas.observables: First-level assignment flips and gradient magnitudes should vary with train-entropy bins; report per-bin item and held-out-transition support with uncertainty intervals, and compare the assignment after norm-matching each transformed latent to its base latent, against a train-only shuffled-profile control. Compare the final Stage3 test Recall@10 with the behaviour-off, geometry-off and both-on runs.

rebuttal.change: Revise the evaluation specification, not the warp: before claiming entropy-stratified transition predictability, report per-bin item and held-out-transition support, uncertainty intervals, and held-out next-item predictability against both behavior-off and a train-only shuffled-profile control; additionally repeat the assignment comparison after norm-matching each transformed latent to its corresponding base latent, and report raw assignments separately. Treat only a shift persisting under norm matching as evidence beyond a simple radial scale change.
rebuttal.remaining: The supplied proxy still has identical both-on and behavior-off assignments [0,0,0] (E15), so mathematical coupling alone establishes neither assignment change nor improved held-out predictability; if the norm-matched audit does not show a persistent effect, a scale-independent branching-structure benefit remains unsupported.
rebuttal.unchanged: The training-only directed predecessor/successor profiles, bounded learned tangent displacement, fixed-curvature Poincare exp/Mobius/log composition, unchanged Euclidean RQ assignments and ordinary training objective remain the proposed mechanism; no score or loss is added.
rebuttal.why: E5's truncated graph counts are no longer offered as the audit: the added, pre-specified held-out, per-entropy-bin audit exposes support and uncertainty and tests predictability directly; norm-matched assignments test whether the observed shift is merely radial scaling while retaining the same profile-driven Poincare warp.

risks: Entropy may mostly encode sparse-count noise or popularity; smoothed q may flatten real branches. Item-specific curvature can create inconsistent distance scales across items, and per-item curvature might shift assignment without useful semantic grouping. Curvature bounds, count shrinkage, and a training-only matched-distance-scale calibration are needed.
ideas.safeguards: Compute geometry in float32; clamp Poincare norms to (1-eps_ball)/sqrt(c_i), with eps_ball around 1e-5; clamp atanh arguments below 1-eps_ball and to nonnegative values; use eps-smoothed probabilities and a bounded log; shrink low-count item distributions toward pi; normalize entropy to [0,1] and clamp c_i to configured bounds. Use stable Mobius addition, gradient clipping, deterministic cached counts, finite-value/gradient tests, and a train-only calibration to keep median curved assignment distance near the baseline scale. For the geometry-off control, use identity/squared Euclidean distance and match score scale on training batches only.
ideas.spec_equations: n_ij=sum_{u,t in train} 1[x_{u,t}=i and x_{u,t+1}=j]; pi_j=(sum_i n_ij+eps)/(sum_{i,j}n_ij+N*eps); q_ij=(n_ij+alpha*pi_j)/(sum_l n_il+alpha); H_i= -sum_j q_ij log(q_ij+eps)/log(max(2,N)); c_i=clip(c_min+(c_max-c_min)H_i,c_min,c_max). For each z_i,a_k: x=exp_0^{c_i}(z_i), y=exp_0^{c_i}(a_k), k*=argmin_k [2/sqrt(c_i) atanh(sqrt(c_i)||(-x)⊕_{c_i}y||)]^2. Compute standard RQ-VAE reconstruction and commitment/codebook losses using selected code; gradients pass through maps and curved distance. Treat zero-count items via smoothed q and the same formula.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: frozen item embeddings, item IDs, train-only user-ordered interaction sequences, encoder output z_i, first-level codebook vectors a_k, alpha, epsilon, and fixed c_min/c_max. Outputs: cached per-item H_i and c_i, first-stage assignment indices, quantized vectors, losses, and final RQ-VAE SID tokens.

specification.text: Count adjacent transitions n_ij within train users' chronologically ordered train events. Let q_ij=(n_ij+alpha*pi_j)/(n_i+alpha), with pi the train next-item frequency, and H_i=-sum_j q_ij log(q_ij+eps)/log(max(2,N)). Set c_i=clamp(c_min+(c_max-c_min)*H_i, c_min,c_max), e.g. c_min=0.1,c_max=1.0. For encoder z_i and codeword a_k, map x_i=exp^{c_i}_0(z_i), y_ik=exp^{c_i}_0(a_k), assign k*=argmin_k d_{c_i}(x_i,y_ik)^2, where d_c(x,y)=2/sqrt(c)*atanh(sqrt(c)*||(-x)⊕_c y||), and train standard reconstruction/VQ commitment losses through the chosen curved quantizer. Use the same c_i for all candidates of item i; later residual levels may remain baseline. Pre-score evidence probe on train only: compare held-out-within-train next-item top-k predictability and branching-bin prefix purity for high- versus low-H items; the hypothesis requires high-H items to have more distinct useful continuation prefixes and expects high-H bin prefix successor coverage to rise under this assignment.

ideas.coupling_path: Train-only co-consumption -> item profile membership r_ik -> anchor-distance term d_c(e_j,a_k)^2 inside the same curved item/code cost as d_c(x_i,e_j)^2 -> Sinkhorn Q -> first-level assignments, gradients, and SID prefixes. Removing either profile term or curved costs changes this cost matrix and its resulting assignments.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Popularity-corrected co-consumption cohorts contain complementary next-item evidence not present in text embeddings. Pre-score train-only probe: on a user-stratified held-out subset of TRAIN interactions, measure whether items assigned to the same first-prefix via this transport yield higher cohort-conditioned next-item Recall@10 than content-only prefixes at comparable prefix occupancy; expect an increase, especially among items with similar content but low profile cosine. Keep only if both-on beats both controls and Stage3 test Recall@10 exceeds 0.065.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: First-level quantization cost matrix before balanced Sinkhorn assignment; its output Q selects the first SID token and affects the codebook/encoder quantization gradients.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare exponential map and negative-curvature (-c, c>0) geodesic distance d_c, used in a behavior-conditioned transport cost; c is one fixed, predeclared curvature (e.g. c=1) for all points.
ideas.key_change: Form K frozen behavior anchors by clustering item vectors built from train-only, popularity-corrected user co-consumption profiles. For each training item, add its Poincare distance to each anchor (weighted by its soft profile membership) to the latent-to-codeword cost, then use a minibatch Sinkhorn assignment on that combined curved cost so code capacity is allocated across distinct cohorts rather than dominated by frequent items.
ideas.leakage_boundary: User-item sets, item frequencies, profile matrix, anchor clustering, and all cached memberships come only from training interactions plus the frozen item inventory/embeddings. Validation/test are evaluation-only; no their interaction, co-consumption, marginal, or assignment contributes to profiles, anchors, Sinkhorn targets, or SID construction.
ideas.motivation: Content-near items can have very different collaborative audiences; a tokenizer that groups only by content can collapse items consumed by distinct user cohorts into shared prefixes, weakening next-item prediction.
ideas.novelty: Rather than transition-direction scoring, branch-conditioned curvature, or a separate pairwise behavior loss, this uses popularity-corrected train-only user co-consumption to define a small set of behavior anchors and performs batch-balanced hyperbolic transport directly into first-level codewords. The transport assignment itself changes prefix membership.
ideas.observables: Measure first-code assignment changes versus baseline, code occupancy/cohort mixing, and the pre-score train-held-out within-prefix next-item Recall@10 (expected to rise for low-content-similarity/high-co-consumption-affinity pairs). Primary outcome is Stage3 test Recall@10; require >0.065 and compare all matched arms.
risks: Co-consumption can reflect exposure/popularity rather than preference; profile sparsity and cohort count K can make anchors unstable. Balanced minibatch marginals may over-regularize genuinely skewed code use, and anchor term can compete with reconstruction. Sinkhorn temperature and lambda require train-only calibration; minibatch composition may add variance.
ideas.safeguards: Exclude diagonal C_ii; require positive df and smooth counts; clip A and retain only top-m positive entries; L2-normalize with epsilon and assign empty profiles to a train-only global fallback membership. Use float32 geometry, project ball norms to at most (1-1e-5)/sqrt(c), clamp atanh inputs below 1-1e-5, and clamp cost logits before exponentiation. Sinkhorn log-domain iterations, epsilon floor, finite checks, gradient clipping, and a fallback to row-wise softmax if marginal scaling fails. Freeze anchors and profile memberships; fix seeds and batch sampling across ablations. Calibrate lambda/eps and report train-only assignment cost and marginal error.
ideas.spec_equations: X_ui=1 if train user u interacted with item i; df_i=sum_u X_ui; C=X^T X; A_ij=log((C_ij+alpha)U/((df_i+alpha)(df_j+alpha))) for i!=j. p_i=normalize(top_m_positive(A_i)); r_i=softmax(-dist_sq(p_i,mu_k)/tau). T_ij=d_c(exp_0^c(z_i),exp_0^c(code_j))^2 + lambda*sum_k r_ik*d_c(exp_0^c(code_j),exp_0^c(anchor_k))^2. Q=diag(u) exp(-T/eps) diag(v), with u,v iteratively scaled to row target 1 and column target B/Kcode. Quantization loss is sum_ij Q_ij ||z_i-code_j||^2 (straight-through output uses argmax Q); reconstruction remains unchanged.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: TRAIN user-item interactions, frozen item embeddings/IDs, encoder outputs z_i, first-level codebook, fixed c, alpha,m,K,lambda,eps; outputs: cached sparse p_i and r_i, anchor points, per-batch Q, selected first-level indices, quantized vectors, and final SIDs.

specification.text: From training users only, create binary user-item matrix X and item co-consumption C=X^T X; set A_ij=log((C_ij+alpha)*U/((df_i+alpha)*(df_j+alpha))) for i!=j, where U is train user count and df_i train-user frequency. Retain each row's top m positive neighbors and L2-normalize to profile p_i. Fit K-means to p_i using train items only to get anchor memberships r_ik (softmax of negative squared profile distances / tau); map each anchor's frozen mean item embedding through exp_0^c to Poincare point a_k. For minibatch encoder z_i and train-only co-consumption profile membership r_i, map z_i and codewords e_j to ball points x_i,e_j; define T_ij=d_c(x_i,e_j)^2 + lambda * sum_k r_ik*d_c(e_j,a_k)^2. Compute entropy-regularized balanced assignment Q=Sinkhorn(exp(-T/eps), row sums 1 and column sums B/K), use argmax_j Q_ij for emitted first code, and train with Q-weighted codebook/commitment loss plus standard reconstruction. Use the same learned codebook at inference; behavior profiles are not required at Stage3.

ideas.title: Popularity-corrected co-consumption transport for hyperbolic prefix allocation

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Set A_ij=0 and lambda_i=0, recovering the unshifted baseline input and ordinary first-level assignment with the same curved quantizer.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Use train-only A_ij, Poincare Karcher anchor/blend, and hyperbolic nearest-code assignment as specified; compare same seeds, training schedule, and Stage3 protocol.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Use Euclidean vectors, Euclidean neighbor mean m_i=x_i+eta sum_j A_ij(x_j-x_i), blend x'_i=(1-lambda_i)x_i+lambda_i m_i, and squared Euclidean code distance; keep graph and all other settings fixed.
ideas.behavior_computation: On the Stage2 training split only, for each user deduplicate their interacted item set S_u. Accumulate C_ij += 1/|S_u| for distinct i,j in S_u. Define A_ij proportional to C_ij/sqrt((d_i+eps)(d_j+eps)), remove self-edges, retain top 32 neighbors per row, and row-normalize. No validation or test records are read.
ideas.behavior_signal: Symmetric user co-consumption, adjusted for global item popularity.
ideas.cost_estimate: Precompute co-consumption graph once from train interactions; retain top 32 neighbors/item. At 24,556 items and 24 steps/epoch, first-level anchor calculation costs at most 24,556*32 curved log-map neighbor operations per epoch (about 0.59M neighbor terms), amortized/precomputed if encoder is frozen only; with changing embeddings recompute once per epoch, not each of 24 batches. Adds about 1.8B neighbor terms over 3000 epochs in the conservative online version, plus negligible top-32 sparse storage; expected wall-clock overhead is concentrated in this per-epoch preprocessing and should be benchmarked. Compared with brute all-pairs, sparse construction is essential.
ideas.coupling_equation: x_i=exp_0^c(e_i); m_i=exp_{x_i}^c(eta sum_j A_ij log_{x_i}^c(x_j)); x'_i=exp_{x_i}^c(lambda_i log_{x_i}^c(m_i)); q_i=argmin_k d_c(x'_i,c_k)^2. Both A_ij (behavior) and log/exp/d_c (curvature) are required for this assignment pathway.
ideas.coupling_path: Train co-consumption weights select neighboring item points; their Poincare log-map average displaces the current item along a curved tangent, which changes its first-level nearest code and hence its SID prefix.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Among items with similar content embeddings, those co-consumed by the same train users should share first-level codes more often, while unrelated cohort items split; the train statistic is the co-consumer edge-versus-nonedge first-level prefix agreement gap, expected to increase. Retain only if Stage3 test Recall@10 exceeds 0.065 and beats both ablations.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: First residual quantizer input, immediately before the first codebook nearest-neighbor assignment; applies while training and when exporting item SIDs using the frozen train graph.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare-ball exp/log maps and distance with fixed curvature c=1 (ball radius (1-eps)/sqrt(c)); the Karcher tangent average is a curved operation.
ideas.key_change: For each item, compute a sparse weighted mean of its train co-consumers in the Poincare ball, and blend that anchor into the encoded vector in tangent coordinates before first-level code selection; later residual levels remain unchanged.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Construct C and A solely from training user histories/interactions. Freeze the graph before fitting/exporting SIDs; validation/test are only used downstream for evaluation and cannot enter graph weights, support counts, anchors, or model selection of individual assignments.
ideas.motivation: Content-near items can serve different user cohorts and should not be forced into the same early SID prefix; training-only co-consumption supplies a collaborative neighborhood signal that can adjust grouping.
ideas.novelty: Unlike directed-transition gates, branch-radius biases, or transition-mass prefix losses, this builds a sparse item-item co-consumption graph and uses its hyperbolic Fréchet (Karcher) anchor directly as an additional candidate in the first residual code assignment. Behavior changes the location being quantized, not just a distance weight or auxiliary loss.
ideas.observables: Measure first-level SID agreement for train co-consumption edges versus degree/popularity-matched nonedges, the fraction of items whose first-level code changes versus content-only baseline, and Stage3 Recall@10. Expected edge/nonedge agreement gap rises without collapsing code usage; goal is test Recall@10 > 0.065.
risks: Popular items may dominate co-consumption; approximate Karcher means may oversmooth useful content distinctions; anchor directions can be noisy for low-support items; recomputing 32 curved maps/item/epoch may cost too much.
ideas.safeguards: Project every ball point to norm <=(1-eps)/sqrt(c), clamp acosh/atanh arguments and conformal factors, accumulate neighbor weights in float32, exclude self edges, normalize nonempty rows, set lambda_i=0 when n_i=0, cap eta and lambda_i to [0,1], and fall back to x_i if any map is nonfinite. Clip gradient norms and test c->0 Euclidean-limit behavior.
ideas.spec_equations: Normalize e_i to x_i=exp_0^c(e_i). For sparse neighbor set N(i), m_i=exp_{x_i}^c(eta sum_{j in N(i)} A_ij log_{x_i}^c(x_j)); x'_i=exp_{x_i}^c(lambda_i log_{x_i}^c(m_i)); q_i=argmin_k d_c(x'_i,c_k)^2. Quantization residual is x'_i minus selected code in log/code tangent coordinates, mapped back consistently; subsequent levels use the repository's normal residual path. Use straight-through gradients through q_i as in baseline.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs are item encoder vectors e_i, train-only sparse normalized neighbor rows A_i, support n_i, first-level codebook {c_k}, curvature c, eta, lambda0, kappa. Output is first-level code index q_i and curved residual passed to later levels; inference/export requires only item ID, frozen encoder, and frozen train graph row.

specification.text: Let e_i be the encoder output mapped by exp_0^c to x_i. Build normalized sparse weights A_ij from train-only user co-consumption. Compute a one-step Karcher approximation m_i=exp_{x_i}^c(eta * sum_j A_ij log_{x_i}^c(x_j)); set x'_i=exp_{x_i}^c(lambda_i log_{x_i}^c(m_i)). Select first-level code argmin_k d_c(x'_i,c_k)^2, then continue ordinary residual quantization. lambda_i=lambda0*n_i/(n_i+kappa), where n_i is co-consumer support, preventing unsupported items from moving.

papers.title: HVQ-VAE: Variational auto-encoder with hyperbolic vector quantization

papers.abstract: The success of models operating on tokenized data has heightened the need for effective tokenization methods, particularly in vision and auditory tasks where inputs are naturally continuous. A common solution is to employ Vector Quantization (VQ) within VQ Variational Autoencoders (VQVAEs), transforming inputs into discrete tokens by clustering embeddings in Euclidean space. However, Euclidean embeddings not only suffer from inefficient packing and limited separation - due to their polynomial volume growth - but are also prone to codebook collapse, where only a small subset of codebook vectors are effectively utilized. To address these limitations, we introduce HyperVQ, a novel approach that formulates VQ as a hyperbolic Multinomial Logistic Regression (MLR) problem, leveraging the exponential volume growth in hyperbolic space to mitigate collapse and improve cluster separability.
